title: Present Perfect and Past Simple/Past Perfect Sentence Completion Exercises
summary: Two grammar exercises: one asks to fill sentences with the present perfect simple or continuous, covering topics like daily activities and questions; the other requires completing sentences using the past simple or past perfect with verbs in brackets.

title: Writing a Brief Holiday Description
summary: A writing task where students plan notes about a holiday using guiding prompts—destination, companions, accommodation, activities, highlights—and then compose a 100–120 word description.

title: Pride and Prejudice Extract: True/False and Comprehension Questions
summary: Exercises based on a Pride and Prejudice extract: students judge statements as true or false and then answer seven comprehension questions about the characters' actions, opinions, and motivations.

title: Pride and Prejudice Vocabulary Matching and Creative Writing
summary: Continues Section 1 with vocabulary exercises where students find synonyms and complete sentences, followed by a creative writing task imagining the dialogue of Mr Bennet's visit to Mr Bingley.

title: Pride and Prejudice Extract: Multiple Choice and True/False Questions
summary: Exercises on a ballroom scene from Pride and Prejudice: students answer multiple-choice questions about Mr Darcy and Elizabeth's exchange, then verify statements as true or false about the characters.

title: Pride and Prejudice Vocabulary, Character Identification and Dialogue Writing
summary: Continues Section 2 with a vocabulary synonym-finding task, a character identification exercise, and an imaginative writing task where students write a conversation between Elizabeth and Mr Darcy.

title: Pride and Prejudice Extract: Ordering Events, Matching and Questions
summary: Exercises based on an extract where Elizabeth overhears the Bingley sisters: students order events chronologically, match characters with their actions, and answer comprehension questions about class and appearance.

title: Pride and Prejudice Vocabulary and Letter-Writing Task
summary: Continues Section 3 with a vocabulary exercise finding synonyms for words in the text, followed by a creative task where students write a letter from Elizabeth's perspective about overhearing the conversation.
